sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds works from Room L116 of the county government center at 669 Washington Street in Easton. Phone 610-829-6210. Staff are at the counter until half past four, but a recording that needs a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m.

The office records, images and stores deeds, mortgages and other real estate papers filed in the county. Each document gets a volume and page reference, then it is imaged for viewing and copying. The office also collects the fees and taxes on property transfers and passes them along.

Sellers meet this office at the very end of a sale. The title company gets the deed signed, carries it to Easton, and the recording puts the buyer's name on the public record. Most deeds need a parcel certification, so a courier who arrives at 4:15 may be told to come back tomorrow.

Filing a deed costs $76.25 on the schedule that began December 1, 2025. That price assumes four pages and four names at most, with parcel certification added on top.

Recording fees, effective December 1, 2025
DocumentFee

Mortgage satisfaction, assignment or release$61.75
Extra page after the fourth$2.00
Extra name after the fourth$0.50

An easement or right of way costs $59.75, and a power of attorney used to sell real estate costs $18.50 plus parcel certification. A Statement of Value costs $2 and counts toward the page total, certifications cost $2.50, and copies are fifty cents a page.

sections.h2: How a closing agent pays the recorder
sections.html:
Make payment out to "Recorder of Deeds." Personal checks are refused. Business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash all work, and a single check can cover five documents at most.

The exact amount has to accompany each document, and the office turns away overpayments. Packages built on a rough guess run into that rule, so build the number line by line from the schedule.

  • Count the pages first, then add $2 for every page past four.
  • Add $10 for each parcel on documents marked with an asterisk on the schedule.
  • Count names past four at $0.50 each.
  • Add the separate transfer tax payment if the deed is taxable.

sections.h2: Paper rules the Easton office enforces
sections.html:
The fee schedule opens with house rules, and they decide whether a deed is recorded or returned.

  • Parcel numbers must appear on every document that relates to real estate. The county's public parcel search is at ncpub.org.
  • Pages should be letter size, 8.5 by 11 inches. A paper that cannot comply, with 8.5 by 14 as the only allowed exception, pays a $10 penalty.
  • Blanket assignments, releases and satisfaction pieces are refused.
  • Anything coming back by mail needs a return envelope with the right postage already on it.

Not every filing is a deed. If a sale involves a new lot line or survey, the county charges $35 for the first page of a subdivision, site or survey plan and $30 for each added page. State highway plans cost $15 for the first page and $3 after that, and a lease for 30 years or longer costs $59.75. Full-size map copies up to 36 by 48 inches are $25.

Every document is microfilmed and open to public inspection, so whatever gets filed in Easton becomes searchable by anyone. Page count drives the fee. A deed with a long legal description and an attached exhibit can pass four pages quickly, so check before you assume the base price.

On a taxable deed the recorder takes the state's 1 percent along with whatever local transfer tax the municipality and school district impose. State rules hold the grantor and the grantee jointly responsible.

The state exempts some deeds, among them certain family transfers, deeds to a government body and inherited property. If you believe your deed fits, tell the title agent early. For the local share, call the recorder's office and give the municipality where the house stands, because the figure can differ from one borough or township to the next.

Who actually pays is a matter for the sales contract, so read that clause before closing.

All of them. Two cities, Bethlehem and Easton, sit among many boroughs and townships, yet every deed for land inside the county line is recorded in the same Easton office. Part of Bethlehem lies in Lehigh County, a different county with its own recorder, so confirm which side your house is on before planning the closing.

Local transfer tax and school district bills follow the municipality, so a sale in Hellertown can price out differently from one in Palmer Township. Other boroughs in the county include Northampton, Wilson, Nazareth, Bangor, Pen Argyl and Wind Gap.

sections.h2: What happens after the deed is recorded
sections.html:
Once the clerk accepts the paper and the fee, the deed is stamped with its volume and page reference and imaged. From that point it is a public record. Your title company usually tracks this step and confirms it to you, and the buyer's lender, if there is one, waits on it before funds are released.

If a deed comes back, the cause is nearly always a missing parcel number, a wrong fee, a page that is the wrong size or an envelope without postage. Fix the item and send it again. Nothing about the sale is lost, but the recording date moves, so tell the buyer's side what happened. As the seller you should bring ID to the signing, the parcel number and the tax certification, so the package leaves the table complete.

Most delays are paper problems, not legal ones. Work through this list a few days ahead.

  • Confirm the parcel number on the deed matches the county's parcel search.
  • Count pages and names to get the exact fee, with no overpayment.
  • Ask whether the title company will deliver by 4:00 p.m., since parcel-certified recordings close early.
  • Pull the tax certification and any unpaid tax before the closing date.
  • Ask the title agent how the Statement of Value is being counted in the page total.
  • Collect a return envelope with correct postage if the deed is coming back by mail.

Open mortgage balances get released through a satisfaction piece, which costs $61.75 to record. Ask the lender how long it takes to file one so the buyer's title is clean. A cash sale skips the lender's recording package, which leaves fewer documents to count and price.

The county has an estimated 324,411 residents as of 2025, with Easton as the seat and Bethlehem as the biggest city. The latest five-year survey shows a $308,600 median home, $89,184 median household income and owners in 71.1 percent of occupied units. Housing costs sit well below Montgomery County to the south.

faqs.q: What will it cost to file a deed in Easton?
faqs.a: Plan on $76.25 for a deed of four pages and four names. Add $10 per certified parcel, $2 for each extra page and 50 cents for each extra name.

faqs.q: Can I pay the recorder with a personal check?
faqs.a: No. The office takes business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash, and caps a check at five documents.

faqs.q: Can I overpay the recording fee?
faqs.a: No. The office wants the exact fee with each document and refuses overpayments, so work out the total before the package goes out.

faqs.q: When does the recorder stop taking documents?
faqs.a: The counter stays open until 4:30 p.m., but anything needing a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m. A later deed waits for the next business day.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: State law makes both sides jointly responsible for the 1 percent state tax. The contract decides who actually pays, so check that clause.
